prompt: The same 8 related concepts, covered two different ways:

options.label: One 2-hour session, all 8 concepts
options.content: Concepts 1-2 land fine while working memory still has room. By concept 4 or 5, new material is competing with everything still being actively juggled from earlier, and comprehension doesn't gently decline - it falls off sharply. The session isn't just failing to add value past that point; the overload actively crowds out consolidation of the earlier concepts too, since working memory never gets a break to hand anything off to longer-term memory.

options.label: Eight 15-minute sessions, one concept each
options.content: Each session stays comfortably within working memory's capacity, so there's room to actually engage with the one idea instead of just holding it in a queue behind others. The gap between sessions also acts as a break that lets each idea get consolidated before the next one arrives. Same total content, same total time - the difference is never overloading the same three-to-five-item buffer that a long session runs straight through.
